title: Stream Control Transmission Protocol
subtitle: A message-oriented transport protocol offering multi-streaming, multi-homing, and ordered/unordered delivery - features TCP and UDP lack.

plainLanguage.summary: SCTP (Stream Control Transmission Protocol) is a transport-layer protocol that delivers messages reliably. It supports multi-streaming, which carries several independent streams in one connection, and multi-homing, which lets an endpoint use several IP addresses. It was originally designed for telephony signaling.

questions: how is sctp different from tcp
why does sctp use a four-way handshake

tldr.problem: TCP delivers one ordered byte stream over one path, so a single lost packet stalls everything and a broken path ends the connection.
tldr.mechanism: An SCTP association carries message-oriented data in several independent streams over one or more IP addresses, set up with a four-way cookie handshake.
tldr.outcome: Loss in one stream does not block the others, and traffic can fail over to another path; SCTP is used for telecom signaling and WebRTC data channels.

facts.label: Handshake
facts.value: 4-way: INIT, INIT ACK, COOKIE ECHO, COOKIE ACK

today: SCTP is used for telecom signaling (SS7 over IP and the 3GPP interfaces) and as the transport for WebRTC data channels, where it runs over DTLS over UDP. It is available in Linux, FreeBSD and other kernels, but is rarely used on the open internet because many NATs and firewalls drop non-TCP/UDP protocols. RFC 4960 has since been obsoleted by RFC 9260, which keeps the same protocol with updates and corrections. QUIC also offers independent streams.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
SCTP (Stream Control Transmission Protocol) is a transport-layer protocol that provides reliable, message-oriented delivery with support for multi-homing and multi-streaming. It was originally designed for telephony signaling (SS7 over IP) but has broader applications.

SCTP combines the reliability of TCP with the message boundaries of UDP, while adding features neither provides: multiple independent streams within a single connection and seamless failover between network paths.
sections.plainLanguage: SCTP is a transport-layer protocol that gives reliable, message-oriented delivery with multi-homing and multi-streaming. It combines TCP's reliability with UDP's message boundaries, and adds multiple independent streams per connection and failover between network paths. It was originally designed for telephony signaling.

sections.plainLanguage: SCTP differs from TCP in several ways. It keeps message boundaries, where TCP sends a byte stream. It supports multiple independent streams and multiple IP addresses per endpoint. Head-of-line blocking, where one lost packet delays later data, applies only within a single stream. Its four-way handshake with a cookie protects against SYN floods.

sections.title: Multi-Streaming
sections.content:
A single SCTP association can carry multiple independent streams. A lost packet in one stream does not block delivery in other streams, solving TCP's head-of-line blocking problem.

QUIC (RFC 9000) also offers independent streams within one connection. WebRTC uses SCTP for its data channel, running SCTP over DTLS over UDP.
sections.plainLanguage: One SCTP association, meaning a connection between two endpoints, can carry several independent streams. A lost packet in one stream does not block delivery in the others, which avoids TCP's head-of-line blocking. WebRTC uses SCTP for its data channel, running SCTP over DTLS over UDP.

sections.title: Multi-Homing
sections.content:
SCTP endpoints can have multiple IP addresses. If the primary path fails, traffic automatically switches to an alternate address without disrupting the connection.

Heartbeat
Periodic probes verify reachability of alternate paths
Failover
Automatic retransmission on alternate path after primary failure
Telecom Use
Valued in telecom signaling, where losing the connection is costly
sections.plainLanguage: SCTP endpoints can have several IP addresses. Periodic heartbeat probes check that alternate paths work. If the primary path fails, traffic switches to an alternate address without breaking the connection. Telecom signaling values this, because losing a connection there is costly.

fields.name: Source Port
fields.desc: The sender's port number. Port 0 must not be used.

fields.name: Destination Port
fields.desc: The port the packet is destined for, used to demultiplex to the right endpoint. Port 0 must not be used.

fields.name: Verification Tag
fields.desc: A 32-bit tag the receiver uses to check the packet belongs to the current association and is not a leftover from an earlier one.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: A CRC32c checksum over the whole packet.

messages.label: INIT ACK
messages.note: Reply with a State Cookie. B keeps no state yet.

messages.label: COOKIE ACK
messages.note: B builds its state and the association is established.
